cosy-lesson.title: Your brain starts making social decisions before you do

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Subconscious – concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences actions.

p.em: Example: Our subconscious mind often processes social cues before we notice them.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pre-emptive – serving or intended to forestall something, especially to prevent an attack.

p.em: Example: The brain's pre-emptive processing helps us avoid social conflict.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive bias – a systematic error in thinking that occurs when people are processing and interpreting information.

p.em: Example: Cognitive bias can lead us to make unfair judgments about new people.

cosy-blockquote.p: Neural firing – the electrical signal that travels along an axon when a neuron is activated.

p.em: Example: Neural firing patterns can predict a social decision seconds before it is made.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cooperation – the process of working together to the same end.

p.em: Example: The study focused on the brain's role in initiating cooperation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intuition – the ability to understand something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

p.em: Example: Social intuition is actually the result of rapid unconscious processing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy ≠ Apathy – the ability to understand other's feelings ≠ a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.

p.em: Example: Hearing people's thoughts taught him true empathy, replacing his lifelong cold apathy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Social cue – a verbal or non-verbal hint, which can be positive or negative, that guides social interaction.

p.em: Example: The brain is highly sensitive to even the smallest social cue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Amygdala – a part of the brain involved with the experiencing of emotions.

p.em: Example: The amygdala plays a central role in our immediate social reactions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Inference – a conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.

p.em: Example: We often make rapid social inferences without having all the facts.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, what neural evidence proves that the brain begins forming subconscious choices before conscious awareness?
★ Complete using inversion: 'Rarely do we realize how much our social decisions are influenced by subcortical brain circuits.'

How does pre-conscious neural firing in neuro-imaging challenge traditional philosophical concepts of free will?
★ Have you ever made an impulsive social decision that you regretted later?

How does the research explain how our subconscious mechanisms execute pre-emptive processing of social interactions?
★ Who do you trust the most in your life, and how did they earn that trust?

According to the study, how does an immediate cognitive bias override rational game-theory choices?
★ Do you find it easy to read other people's body language and emotions?

Why did ancestral human networks evolve to prioritize pre-conscious cooperation over slower logical calculations?
★ Have you ever felt peer pressure to agree with a group decision you disliked?

How does the article describe the neural path through which our intuition interprets even the smallest social cue?
★ How quickly do you form a first impression of someone you just met?

How does the activation of the amygdala trigger emotional reactions that compete directly with rational inference?
★ Do you think your subconscious mind plays a big role in your everyday choices?

What empirical evidence does the article present to link high empathy with rapid unconscious social inference?
★ What is the most difficult social decision you have had to make recently?

According to the research, under what circumstances can cold apathy override the brain's natural push toward cooperation?
★ Do you find that stress makes you make more rational or more emotional decisions?

How does the study use neuroeconomics to show that pre-emptive insula signals predict the rejection of unfair agreements?
★ How do you feel when you have to make a choice with very little information?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this study, how will psychologists adjust our understanding of "free will" and subconscious social mechanics?
★ Would you trust an algorithm to recommend who you should date or marry?

Imagine future research proves that pre-emptive neural choices are fully automated and unalterable. Will the concept of moral responsibility disappear?
★ Do you think advertising is so psychologically advanced that we don't have free will anymore?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to artificially adjust amygdala responses. Will we succeed in permanently eliminating negative cognitive bias in society?
★ Should schools teach cognitive biases to help children make better logical decisions?

If future research continues to show that neural firing can predict complex social choices minutes in advance, will we use real-time brainwave monitoring to optimize group cooperation?
★ Would you use an app that analyzes your friends' voices to tell you if they are lying?

Imagine future neuro-implants allow us to override our subconscious intuition. Will this lead to more rational decisions, or will we lose our human empathy?
★ Do you think social media has made people more or less trusting of each other?

If future research proves that a lack of cooperation is a purely biological byproduct of insula apathy, how will we adjust our leadership selection standards?
★ Would you let a computer select the most qualified job candidates for your company?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, if we prove that social media platforms are directly exploiting subconscious neural firing, will we design biological neural filters?
★ What is the best way to train your mind to think slowly and avoid hasty judgments?

Imagine future AI models simulate human social inference and find that trust relies entirely on rapid social cues. What new social networks might they construct?
★ Do you believe that some people are naturally born with better social intuition than others?

If future research continues to prove that empathy can be chemically simulated to boost trust, will this lead to a major philosophical split in how we value authentic connections?
★ How can we rebuild social trust in communities where people are highly divided?

As our understanding of pre-emptive amygdala signals grows, will we finally develop technology that can predict and prevent interpersonal conflicts before they occur?
★ If you could see a real-time graph of your stress levels, would you use it to make decisions?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am not aware about it → Correct: I am not aware of it ((Aware + of))
Incorrect: The brain decide very fast → Correct: The brain decides very fast ((Subject-verb agreement))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
Incorrect: I have 25 years old → Correct: I am 25 years old ((Age with 'to be'))
